newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bills end firmer but holiday stifles NZ debt mkts.
newsitem.headline: Bills end firmer but holiday stifles NZ debt mkts.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.60 PCT (PREV 7.60) US 5-YR 6.30 (PREV 6.33) NZD/USD 0.7071/78 (PREV 0.7091/98) US 10-YR 6.55 (PREV 6.56)
* Price making in NZ debt mkts affected by Wgtn bank holiday * Short end better-bid with TWI at record highs
There was no price making to move Zealand debt markets on Monday because of a bank holiday in Wellington, although dealers said the bank bills had firmed a touch through broker activity.
"It's dead quiet with Wellington being out," an Auckland dealer said. "There's actually no price-making today. It's sort of a gentlemen's agreement."
However, dealers said the short end was better bid as the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index reached levels not seen since late 1987.
"The only thing that can really be said is that the futures were a touch stronger just on the back of the TWI," said another dealer.
He said the bond market was devoid of even broker activity and hadn't moved at all.
